basis: Congenital cardiac defects and hand skeletal malformations define the syndrome and are obligate findings.
Immune-mediated food hypersensitivity; acute gastrointestinal symptoms, urticaria and shock do not establish persistent organ damage.
Lissencephaly defines disease; finger skeletal deformity in 10/24 (~42%). Cardiac morphology abnormalities in 6/27 (<30%) despite a broader frequent annotation.
Squamous carcinoma confined to the epidermis; no invasion or other organ involvement.
Surviving mosaic cases commonly have congenital cardiac and limb/skeletal malformations; complete trisomy 16 is generally embryonically lethal. Phenotype data are absent.
Necrotizing bacterial infection destroys soft tissues, typically skin, subcutis and fascia; muscle involvement varies by subtype.
Dermal collagen nevi define disease. Cardiac abnormalities are occasional (5-29%); other extracutaneous findings lack qualifying frequencies.
Carcinoma originates in the sublingual salivary gland, which belongs to the gastrointestinal axis.
Site-unspecified histologic umbrella: anaplasia does not identify an organ of origin, and the heterogeneous subtypes do not justify a shared organ label.
Inherited defects of neurotransmitter metabolism or transport define metabolic disorders of nervous system function.
Congenital absence of an upper limb; explicitly non-syndromic.
Tuberculous infection directly inflames the pericardium. Pulmonary tuberculosis is not inherent to this extrapulmonary concept.
Margarita-type ectodermal dysplasia features hair/nail and dental abnormalities with cleft lip/palate; additional skeletal involvement is insufficiently quantified.
Oligodontia is universal; sparse scalp hair and absent eyebrows each occur in 3/5 (60%). Cancer predisposition alone does not establish additional organ damage.
Malignant neoplasm originates in chest wall bones; thoracic location alone does not establish pulmonary involvement.
GSD Ib causes neutropenia and neutrophil dysfunction; hepatic glycogen disease occurs in most (>80%). Renal and intestinal involvement omitted at the four-axis cap.
Intellectual disability and urethral malformation define disease; joint stiffness 80-99%, nail defects 30-79%. Palatal abnormalities omitted at the four-axis cap.
Benign smooth muscle tumor originates in the appendix; visceral smooth muscle does not imply skeletal muscle disease.
Hypothalamic-pituitary vasopressin deficiency defines an endocrine disorder; polyuria does not establish kidney damage, and neurologic symptoms are not persistent injury.
Noise exposure directly damages the auditory apparatus and causes hearing loss.
Motor neuron disease with muscle atrophy in essentially all patients; congenital contractures in 15/20 (75%) and scoliosis in 12/20 (60%).
Primary breast carcinoma; breast has no axis. Receptor negativity does not make this an endocrine gland disorder.
Folate metabolism/transport disorder with megaloblastic anemia; parent explicitly identifies immunodeficiency, although immune phenotypes are not supplied.
Defining cleft affects the upper lip and premaxillary bone. Nasal, ocular and CNS abnormalities are variable without qualifying frequencies.
Definition identifies neurodevelopmental/CNS and ocular abnormalities as characteristic. Individual defects vary; other organ abnormalities are occasional (5-29%).
